text:
marco: Quick sync — I'm prototyping a gateway fallback chain for capacity-constrained routes. Goal: try primary model, then a quantized variant, then a hosted cheap model, then gracefully fail. Also want header-based overrides and a circuit-breaker to avoid thrashing. Any concerns?

anya: Sounds good. Do we want the fallback decision to be based on quota consumption, instance queue length, or a simple rejection from runtime? All of those have different telemetry implications.

marco: Ideally we route on a combined signal: runtime returns 'capacity=constrained' OR queue_depth > 50 OR infra returns 503. For quota we should be careful — we don't want to bypass billing/limits accidentally.

rachel: From Console POV we need a clear way to visualize fallbacks per-route and toggle the header override. UX ask: a per-route "degradation policy" card showing fallback hits, p95 delta, and open-circuit events. Also a canary toggle.

anya: Agreed. Draft routing policy (for prototyping):
```yaml
match:
  path: /v1/generate
  header:
    x-rw-model: redwood-l2
policy:
  routing:
    primary: redwood-l2
    fallback_order:
      - redwood-l2-quant
      - redwood-mini-hosted
  overrides:
    add_headers:
      x-rw-degraded: "true"
circuit:
  open_if:
    error_rate_5xx: 0.01  # open if >1% 5xx over window
    p95_latency_ms: 2000  # or p95 > 2s
  window_s: 60
  cooldown_s: 30
```

sre-ops: Those thresholds might be aggressive for some customers. Proposal: make thresholds templated by "customer_tier" claim or route annotation. Eg. dedicated customers get higher tolerances. Also add hysteresis: require two consecutive windows to open.

marco: Good call. Let's make circuit parameters overridable per-customer via `x-rw-customer-tier` in JWT claim. Also we will emit these metrics: `gateway.fallback.count`, `gateway.circuit.open`, `gateway.fallback.latency.delta_ms`.

anya: Important: we must preserve request headers and trace propagation when we switch models. Please ensure we forward `x-rw-trace` and `x-request-id` and add `x-rw-fallback-reason` with values: capacity|quota|error.

rachel: For rollout UX — Console should let product teams define a fallback policy and preview on a sample request. Also surface cost delta estimates when fallback to hosted model occurs.

marco: On implementation: gateway will try primary via gRPC, if response contains `x-rw-capacity: constrained` or we get a 503, we consult fallback_order and attempt sequentially. If all fail, respond 429 with structured JSON explaining chain and metric ids.

anya: One more: tests. Unit test for header overrides, integration test that simulates queue backpressure and asserts fallback happened, and e2e canary that flips `x-rw-model` and ensures telemetry shows fallback count increment.

deploy-bot: preview-deploy pipeline started for branch `feature/fallback-chain` — https://ci.redwood.internal/preview/4572

sre-ops: We'll add alerts: when `gateway.circuit.open` > 0.1% of routes in last 5m -> pager. Also alert if fallback rate spikes > 5% of requests.

marco: Ok I will iterate on the YAML and push a PR. Thanks everyone — will tag you when the preview is up.

anya: Ping me when PR is ready, I'll add telemetry hooks and a test harness.

rachel: I'll mock the Console cards so we can show PMs in the next sprint demo.

marco: (also adding a note) we should not expose `x-rw-degraded` to public clients by default; only internal logs and customer admins should see it. Add `x-rw-degraded` to response only when `x-rw-internal=true`.
